items.title: Show HN: I benchmarked 6 MCP proxies in Claude Code, then built my own
items.contentSnippet:
I compared 6 MCP proxies inside Claude Code. Most advertise 85–99% token savings, but those numbers assume every tool schema is loaded upfront, and Claude Code already avoids that. On real tasks, 4 of them used more tokens than no proxy at all, and 2 couldn't finish the tasks. So I built my own router, which cut tokens by 13–44% and completed every task.
Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50124411

items.title: Show HN: Pogi – AWS, Google Cloud and Azure on your machine, in one binary
items.contentSnippet:
I built pogi to test cloud code locally without an emulator per service or a test account. It's one Go binary that serves 181 services across AWS, Google Cloud and Azure on one port.
The official SDKs, CLIs, Terraform and the CDK work unchanged, and there's a web console, IAM checks, chaos rules, snapshots built in and much more...

items.title: Show HN: Donut Browser, the most private anti-detect browser
items.contentSnippet:
Hi everyone!
About 2 years ago, I began to work on Donut Browser as a tool to manage browser profiles, which over time has evolved into a proper anti-detect browser.
Anti-detect browsers let you create browser profiles that look like as if you have a completely different computer. I believe Donut is the most private anti-detect browser because:
- It has no telemetry and doesn't track your browsing activity
- It spoofs your browser identity in a way that looks like a real device for every profile
